heroHeadline: Trump Hosts Artemis II Crew at White House — First Presidential Reception for Lunar Astronauts Since Apollo Era
heroSubtitle: Apr 29-30: In Rabat, Morocco on April 29, Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita and U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau signed the Artemis Accords, making Morocco the 64th nation and fifth African country to commit to peaceful, transparent civil space exploration — a ceremony that coincided with the 250th anniversary of U.S.-Moroccan diplomatic ties and reflected international momentum following Artemis II's April 1–10 crewed lunar flyby. Meanwhile at KSC, the Artemis III SLS core stage was positioned horizontally in the VAB transfer aisle, awaiting imminent vertical lift into High Bay 2 for integration, while Artemis II Orion de-servicing operations continued at the MPPF (avionics extraction, propellant offload underway); NASA clarified the formal heat shield X-ray scans and Avcoat sample extractions will be conducted at Marshall Space Flight Center during summer 2026, after visual inspections conclude at KSC. On April 30, Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, and Mission Specialists Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen made their first late-night television appearance on NBC's The Tonight Show with Jimmy Fallon — day 30 post-splashdown — recounting humanity's first crewed journey to the Moon's vicinity since Apollo 17 in 1972 to an estimated 4–5 million viewers. The crew continues week-five physiological reconditioning at JSC with metrics largely normalized. Starship V3 (Flight 12) received FAA flight-safety approval in late April 2026, with launch from Starbase Pad 2 now targeting May 2026; IFT-12 will validate docking port and propellant-transfer hardware as a prerequisite for orbital refueling demonstrations required for the Artemis III HLS mission profile.
